requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: The binding limit for a fast design is expected to be the plating margin (anode >=25 mV at high C-rate), with peak temperature <=45 degC second; the immediate unknown limiting any forecast-based design is thermal-model mismatch in this fixture, which a 1.5C charge plus 60 min cooling rest exposes at maximum signal-to-noise. Heating during charge and the cooling ratio during rest together inform the thermal fit.

No baseline, no completed results, and no fitted model exist yet (budget 12 remaining). Version 0 is the engineer's calibration in another fixture, so its temperature/anode forecasts cannot be trusted for this fixture until compared with lab data. A uniform 1.5C charge at the stated 25 degC ambient setpoint, inside the 0.2-1.5C bounds and 23-27 degC validity range, gives the largest heating signal and, with the 60 min rest, a cooling trace for thermal fitting. Charge time is deterministic from the steps: 4 x 0.175/1.5 h = 28.0 min. Wide temperature intervals reflect the unknown fixture mismatch, not a measurement.

requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: The binding constraints for a faster design are expected to be plating (min_anode_potential >=25 mV) first and max_temperature <=45 degC second, but neither can be assessed from the lab test alone. The limiting unknown is fixture thermal mismatch: the measured trace in res_9102840609d5078abba3296e peaked at 40.79 degC and returned to temperature_end 24.96 degC after the 60 min rest, far below my predicted 28.0 degC [25.5, 36.0], consistent with substantially stronger cooling than the nominal h=6.0 W/m^2/K. Charge time also missed prediction (29.35 min vs 28.0 [27.5, 28.5]). A family-2 fit can capture h and thermal-mass scale jointly, though the rest trace alone fixes mainly their ratio.

Only one lab test exists (res_9102840609d5078abba3296e) with maximum heating signal at uniform 1.5C and a 60 min cooling rest. Its rapid return to ambient (24.96 degC) versus prediction indicates nominal-model thermal mismatch. Fitting family 2 on test 1 (fit_on=1) is the direct way to obtain a fixture-specific model version for later anode-potential forecasts; version 0 was calibrated in another fixture and cannot yet be trusted for the >=25 mV plating constraint.

Hypothesis: The binding constraint for a fast design is expected to be plating (min_anode_potential >=25 mV), with max_temperature <=45 degC second, but anode margin is only a forecast. The limiting uncertainty is whether the fixture-specific thermal fit (version 1: h=15.022 W/m2/K, k=1.0, 95% region h 14.948-15.095, k 0.99-1.01, fit_adequate yes, nominal inconsistent) generalizes beyond the single uniform-1.5C test it fitted. A stepped decreasing-rate charge tests heating and cooling at several rates and should expose a rate-dependent mismatch if one exists.

Compare prior prediction first: in res_9102840609d5078abba3296e, charge_time_80 missed (29.35 min vs 28.0 [27.5,28.5]) and temperature_end missed (24.96 degC vs 28.0 [25.5,36.0]), while max_temperature was inside (40.79 vs 38.0 [31,46]). In res_6509804b853f8dd08e7f81d1, h and k predictions were inside, but thermal_fit_rmse missed low (0.1471 vs 0.4 [0.15,1.0]); that tightens surface-temperature confidence for the fitted test but does not validate version 1 on a new protocol, and surface agreement cannot validate anode potential. Version 1 fitted only test 1 at 1.5C/25C/60 min rest. This held-out 1.5/1.2/0.9/0.6C test at 25C with 60 min rest stays inside the 0.2-1.5C bounds and 23-27C validity ambient range, varies heating rate to help separate thermal mass from cooling, and uses the 29.35/28.0 scale seen in test 1 for the charge-time prediction: nominal stepped time 44.9 min, predicted 47.0 min.

Hypothesis: The binding constraint for a fast design is expected to be plating (min_anode_potential >= 25 mV) first, with max_temperature <= 45 degC second, but the anode margin is only a forecast. The limiting uncertainty is whether the fixture-specific thermal fit (version 1, h=15.022 W/m2/K) generalizes from the uniform 1.5C test it fitted to a stepped-rate charge; if it does, its forecasts can be used for design.

Compare prior prediction first: test 2 (res_58c7676e25e90e2b260c647c) fell inside all intervals — charge_time_80 44.92 min vs 47.0 [44.0, 50.0], max_temperature 36.46 degC vs 37.0 [30.0, 43.0], temperature_end 24.83 degC vs 25.0 [24.5, 26.5] — consistent with stronger fixture cooling, but a lab test measures only surface temperature and cannot validate anode potential. Version 1 (res_6509804b853f8dd08e7f81d1) fitted only test 1 (fit_on=1, uniform 1.5C, 25 degC, 60 min rest) with thermal_fit_rmse 0.1471 delta_degC, fit_adequate yes, nominal inconsistent, 95% region h 14.948-15.095, k 0.99-1.01. Test 2 varied rates 1.5/1.2/0.9/0.6C at 25 degC and was not fitted, so checking version 1 on test_on=2 is the held-out validation required before any optimize_protocol recommendation under version 1. Predicted held-out RMSE near the fitted 0.1471 degC and the stated 0.15 degC noise if the lumped h/k mechanism generalizes across rates.

Hypothesis: Plating margin (min_anode_potential >= 25 mV) will bind first, forcing a taper at higher SOC, while max_temperature <= 45 degC will be secondary because this fixture cools much more strongly than nominal (fitted h=15.022 W/m^2/K vs nominal 6.0) and even a uniform 1.5C lab charge peaked at only 40.79 degC in res_9102840609d5078abba3296e.

Compare prior prediction first: check_model on held-out test 2 (res_affb085c6102c704c82d373a) fell inside all intervals — heldout_rmse 0.1503 delta_degC vs 0.15 [0.05, 0.4], heldout_max_error 0.4643 vs 0.5 [0.2, 1.0], heldout_coverage 0.9571 vs 0.95 [0.8, 1.0]. That satisfies the requirement to check version 1 on a test it did not fit (test 2, res_58c7676e25e90e2b260c647c) before designing under it. Version 1 (res_6509804b853f8dd08e7f81d1) had fit_adequate yes, nominal inconsistent, thermal_fit_rmse 0.1471 delta_degC, and a tight 95% region (h 14.948-15.095, k 0.99-1.01), so member spread should be small and a robust design plausible. Surface-temperature agreement does not validate the anode potential, so the design's plating margin remains a version-1 forecast, not a measurement. Ambient 25 degC matches the objective setpoint, both lab tests, and version 1's validity range (25 degC, up to 1.5C); it is not an extrapolation. With 8 experiments remaining, a design search now is the highest-value step: it directly tests whether a faster-than-uniform-taper protocol can satisfy anode >= 25 mV and temperature <= 45 degC for every member.

Hypothesis: Plating margin binds the design: the optimize_protocol result res_16c937c7ab61f996e8f1f7ae gives min_anode_potential 26.125 mV, only 1.125 mV above the 25 mV limit, while max_temperature 37.564 degC is 7.436 degC below the 45 degC limit. Temperature is therefore expected to pass comfortably in the lab; the unverified risk is thermal-model mismatch changing the real temperature (and, by forecast only, the anode margin).

Compare prior prediction first: optimize_protocol missed charge_time_80 (47.444 min vs 32.0 [27.0, 40.0]) and c_rate_4 (0.5 vs 1.0 [0.6, 1.5]), while min_anode_potential (26.125 vs 27.0 [25.0, 38.0]) and max_temperature (37.564 vs 40.0 [35.0, 45.0]) were inside. I now believe the anode constraint forces a much stronger late taper (0.5C in the last step) than I assumed, making the feasible design substantially slower. Version 1 was checked on held-out test 2 (res_affb085c6102c704c82d373a: heldout_rmse 0.1503 delta_degC, coverage 0.9571), so designing under it was justified, but a lab test of the actual design rates is the next decision-changing check: it measures surface max_temperature (forecast 37.564 degC; held-out test 2 forecast was 0.355 degC below observed, hence the 37.9 degC prediction) and the realised charge time. Rates are within 0.2-1.5C bounds and ambient 25 degC is within the 23-27 degC validity range, so this is not an extrapolation. A lab test cannot measure anode potential, so the >=25 mV margin remains a version-1 forecast regardless of outcome.

Hypothesis: Plating margin binds the candidate: the optimize_protocol design in res_16c937c7ab61f996e8f1f7ae has min_anode_potential 26.125 mV, only 1.125 mV above the 25 mV limit, while max_temperature 37.564 degC is 7.436 degC below the 45 degC limit. The remaining decision-limiting uncertainty is whether version 1's thermal forecasts generalize to the actual design rates (1.5/1.35/0.9/0.5C), because the anode margin is only a forecast and rests on that thermal model.

Compare prior prediction first: the lab test of the design (res_49a5c82b3d2a48dddf303068) fell inside all intervals — charge_time_80 47.44 min vs 47.4 [46.0, 49.5], max_temperature 37.67 degC vs 37.9 [36.5, 39.5], temperature_end 25.32 degC vs 25.0 [24.5, 26.5] — supporting version 1 at the design rates, but that comparison used only summary maxima, not the full surface-temperature trace. Version 1 (res_6509804b853f8dd08e7f81d1, h=15.022 W/m2/K, k=1.0, fit_adequate yes, thermal_fit_rmse 0.1471 delta_degC) was fitted only on test 1 and already checked on held-out test 2 (res_affb085c6102c704c82d373a: heldout_rmse 0.1503 delta_degC, coverage 0.9571). Test 3 (the 1.5/1.35/0.9/0.5C design charge, res_49a5c82b3d2a48dddf303068) is a new lab test version 1 did not fit, at rates and ambient 25 degC inside its validity range, so checking it (test_on=4, bitmask for test 3) is a genuine held-out validation of the exact candidate protocol. Surface-temperature agreement still cannot validate anode potential; the >=25 mV margin remains a version-1 forecast.

conclusion.text:
Candidate protocol from optimize_protocol res_16c937c7ab61f996e8f1f7ae (rq_3a41a1694b5c38bbf3c5) under model version 1: 1.5 / 1.35 / 0.9 / 0.5 C at 25 degC, forecast charge_time_80 47.444 min, min_anode_potential 26.125 mV (>= 25 mV, margin 1.125 mV) and max_temperature 37.564 degC (<= 45 degC, margin 7.436 degC) for every model member; it meets the constraints in simulation. Speed is not compared: there is no computational baseline meeting the constraints and this objective runs no reference search, so it is not claimed faster than a reference and is not claimed optimal.

Model basis: family-2 thermal fit res_6509804b853f8dd08e7f81d1 gave h=15.022 W/m2/K, k=1.0, fit_adequate yes, nominal inconsistent, thermal_fit_rmse 0.1471 degC. Version 1 was checked on tests it did not fit: held-out test 2 in res_affb085c6102c704c82d373a (heldout_rmse 0.1503 degC, coverage 0.9571) and on the design protocol itself in res_97217d25b41f4b9fffb326af (rq_c7715ba126e71c1df74e: heldout_rmse 0.1453 degC vs predicted 0.15 [0.05, 0.4], heldout_max_error 0.4793 degC vs 0.5 [0.2, 1.0], heldout_coverage 0.9767 vs 0.95 [0.8, 1.0] — all inside prediction).

Lab verification of the design: lab_charge res_49a5c82b3d2a48dddf303068 measured charge_time_80 47.44 min and max_temperature 37.67 degC, both inside prediction. The plating constraint remains a version-1 forecast only: no lab test measures anode potential, and surface-temperature agreement does not validate the anode potential or core temperature.
unresolved_reasons: min_anode_potential (>=25 mV) is never measured in the lab; the candidate's 26.125 mV margin rests solely on the model-version-1 forecast (res_16c937c7ab61f996e8f1f7ae), with only 1.125 mV above the limit.

Speed is not compared: no feasible computational baseline exists and this objective runs no reference search (comparison cmp_edcac23b911d994d28a9b084, verdict inconclusive), so the design is feasible under the model but not shown faster than any reference and not proven fastest possible.

learning.standing_rule: a model version stands behind a design when its fit, if it has one, met the adequacy rule (RMSE at most 2 x the noise, floor 0.3 K) and a check on tests it did not fit, in the lab where the design would run, met the same rule, with no such check failing it or failing to run; a check on the supplied records alone (an earlier fixture) is reported, but neither gives nor takes standing for a lab design
